Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 13, 2026) - NuGen Medical Devices Inc. (TSXV: NGMD) ("NuGen" or the "Company"), a developer of needle-free drug delivery technology, provides an update regarding its Canadian medical device licence for the InsuJet™ needle-free insulin injection system.

Further to the Company's news release dated February 5, 2026, Health Canada has issued a Notice of Refusal in respect of the Company's Class II medical device licence application no. 407982. As previously disclosed, the Company's prior Canadian medical device licence had lapsed and sales in Canada were halted while the new application was under review. Sales and further supply of InsuJet in Canada remain halted.

Health Canada determined that the clinical evidence submitted with the application was insufficient to demonstrate compliance with certain safety and effectiveness requirements under sections 11, 12 and 13 of the Canadian Medical Devices Regulations. The matters identified by Health Canada include the need for additional evidence concerning insulin-specific clinical performance, bioequivalence or alternatively evidence supporting the safety and effectiveness of insulin therapy using the device, longer-term glycemic control and safety endpoints, reliable patient self-administration, and injection performance.

The Notice of Refusal applies to the Canadian application and does not, by itself, amend the regulatory status of InsuJet in jurisdictions outside Canada. NuGen continues to maintain registrations and commercial activities in a number of markets outside Canada, subject in each case to applicable local regulatory requirements.

The Notice of Refusal does not state that InsuJet is unsafe or ineffective. It states that the evidence submitted was insufficient to demonstrate that the requirements applicable to the Canadian application and its proposed use with NovoRapid insulin had been met. Investors should not interpret this distinction as an assurance that a future Canadian application will be approved.

Canadian Market and Existing Users

Based on discussions with the Company's Canadian regulatory representative, the Notice of Refusal does not require a recall of InsuJet devices previously lawfully imported and sold in Canada while the applicable licence was active. The Company has also been advised that existing Canadian users are not required to discontinue use of devices already supplied.

Clinical Evidence and Regulatory Path Forward

NuGen intends to review the Notice of Refusal with its regulatory and clinical advisers and to continue discussions with Health Canada concerning the evidence that may be required for a future submission. Subject to available funding, final protocol design, regulatory feedback and other factors, the Company currently intends to incorporate relevant elements of Health Canada's feedback into clinical evidence-generation activities in connection with its next-generation needle-free injector platform.

Management Comment

"We are disappointed with Health Canada's decision, but the Notice of Refusal provides greater clarity regarding the additional clinical evidence required for a future Canadian application," said Liang Lin, Chief Executive Officer of NuGen. "We intend to consider these requirements as part of our planned clinical program for our next-generation needle-free technology. While sales and further supply in Canada remain halted, we remain committed to working with our regulatory and clinical partners to address Health Canada's requirements and pursue a path back to the Canadian market."

About NuGen Medical Devices

NuGen develops next-generation needle-free devices for subcutaneous drug delivery. Its flagship InsuJet™ system has been registered in numerous international markets and is designed to provide an alternative to conventional needle-based injections.

HOUSTON, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cerenome, Inc. (Nasdaq: CNSY) (“Cerenome” or the “Company”), a CNS oncology company advancing an integrated platform that combines precision diagnostics, targeted radiopharmaceuticals, and artificial intelligence, announces financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provides an overview of recent business progress.

“Recognition of our first quarter of CNSide® diagnostic revenue and commercial payments beginning in October is a tremendous landmark,” said Marc H. Hedrick, M.D., Cerenome’s President and Chief Executive Officer. “Furthermore, our payer universe continues to expand with now about 80% of U.S. private payers representing approximately 190 million covered lives. Most recently, with Aetna coverage, it gives physicians an in-network option for both tumor cell enumeration and molecular profiling. In parallel, our growing commercial team is focused on helping more cancer centers use our test in patient care. In therapeutics, we materially advanced our two key programs by completing enrollment in our Phase 2 trial in adults with recurrent glioblastoma, opening up higher dose cohorts in the repeat dosing of REYOBIQ™ in patients with leptomeningeal metastases and reporting interim data in that trial.”

Q3 2026 AND RECENT HIGHLIGHTS

Corporate

  • During the quarter, Plus Therapeutics rebranded as Cerenome, and on August 3 its common stock began trading on Nasdaq under the symbol CNSY. The new name and brand reflect the Company’s focus on integrating CNS diagnostics, therapeutics, and data.
  • In November, Ron Andrews was appointed as Chief Business Officer to advance CNSide commercial adoption and strategic partnerships. Mr. Andrews continues to serve on the Company’s Board of Directors.

CNSide® CSF Assay Platform

  • The company submitted billing claims for approximately $1.55 million in gross billings at list prices and recognized $0.7 million in net diagnostic revenue in the quarter after estimated payer adjustments and price concessions.
  • Contracted coverage was expanded through agreements with Medical Mutual, Health Care Service Corporation and Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan.
  • Secured in-network agreements were also made with Florida Blue and Aetna. The Aetna agreement, effective November 1, is the first national CNSide payer agreement to include both tumor cell enumeration and molecular profiling. The Company’s aggregate contracted footprint now represents approximately 190 million covered lives.
  • The company entered into a collaboration with Genomic Testing Cooperative to add DNA and RNA profiling to CNSide. In July, the Company also highlighted updated NCCN CNS Cancers Guidelines recognizing a role for CSF analysis in the assessment of LM.
  • XiFin was selected for revenue cycle management and clearinghouse services, and Samantha Fowlkes was appointed as Vice President and Head of Commercial Sales for CNSide Diagnostics.
  • The Company is on track for Medicare reimbursement in 1st half of 2027 and is separately pursuing a coverage determination from Novitas Solutions.
  • CNSide CSF Molecular Profile tests were launched for solid tumors and hematologic malignancies. The test was available to order beginning October 12, providing DNA and RNA profiling from cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). CNSide can be ordered independently or alongside tumor cell enumeration.

REYOBIQ™ Development

  • The company presented interim Phase 1 ReSPECT-LM (multi-dose) findings at the Society of Neuro Oncology Annual meeting in November. The first 10 patients have been treated with repeated intraventricular doses of REYOBIQ, with no dose-limiting toxicities or treatment discontinuations due to adverse events reported. This highlights the potential for REYOBIQ to safely administer higher dose of tumor-destroying radiation (compared to single-dose study). Dose escalation is ongoing to identify a recommended multiple-dose regimen for a follow-on randomized study.
  • Also, enrollment was completed in the Phase 2 ReSPECT-GBM study in recurrent glioblastoma in October. Cerenome expects topline data in mid-2027 following additional patient follow-up, and plans to hold an End-of-Phase 2 meeting with the FDA thereafter.
  • Investigators reported preclinical data at the Rivkin Ovarian Cancer Research Symposium in October showing the active agent in REYOBIQ was associated with a new mechanism of action, namely positively impacting the tumor environment. The net effect described by investigators was administering REYOBIQ along with anti-PD-1 checkpoint blockade enhanced antitumor activity in these preclinical studies, opening up the possibility of novel combination therapies.
  • Investigators presented pharmacokinetic, dosimetry, and safety observations from the ReSPECT-LM program at the SNO/ASCO CNS Metastases Conference in August. A separate presentation examined the potential health economic impact of earlier detection of leptomeningeal metastases (LM) using CNSide.

THIRD QUARTER 2026 FINANCIAL RESULTS

  • Cash, cash equivalents and investments totaled $4.9 million as of September 30, 2026, compared with $8.6 million as of June 30, 2026. In September, the Company announced closing a senior secured financing facility up to $20 million with royalty-based repayments. In addition, the Company raised $3.8M under the Equity Distribution Agreement subsequent to the end of the quarter.
  • Total revenue was $0.7 million, consisting entirely of net diagnostic revenue.
  • Cost of revenue was $0.9 million. Research and development expense was $2.1 million, compared with $2.4 million a year earlier. Selling, general and administrative expense was $5.2 million, compared with $3.4 million a year earlier.
  • Operating loss was $7.5 million, compared with $4.5 million a year earlier. Net loss was $8.7 million, or $1.14 per share, compared with $4.4 million, or $1.03 per share, a year earlier.

ANTICIPATED MILESTONES AND OUTLOOK FOR 2027

CNSide Commercial Rollout

  • Expand CNSide adoption across cancer centers, build-out the field sales team, enhance the testing menu and build on existing payer collection experience across the CNSide test menu.

REYOBIQ Clinical Program

  • Continue dose escalation in LM Multi-dose study and follow patients in ReSPECT-GBM for the anticipated mid-2027 topline readouts from both trials.

About Leptomeningeal metastases (LM)
Leptomeningeal metastases (LM) are a rare but severe complication of advanced cancer, affecting the fluid-lined structures of the central nervous system. LM occurs in approximately 5% of patients with metastatic cancer, with breast cancer, lung cancer, and melanoma being the most common sources. Median survival is typically 2-6 months, and effective treatment options are limited, highlighting the urgent need for novel therapies.

About REYOBIQ™ (rhenium Re186 obisbemeda)
REYOBIQ (rhenium Re186 obisbemeda) is a novel injectable radiotherapy specifically formulated to deliver direct targeted high-dose radiation in CNS tumors in a safe, effective, and convenient manner to optimize patient outcomes. REYOBIQ has the potential to reduce off-target risks and improve outcomes for CNS cancer patients versus currently approved therapies, with a more targeted and potent radiation dose. Rhenium-186 is an ideal radioisotope for CNS therapeutic applications due to its short half-life, beta energy for destroying cancerous tissue, and gamma energy for real-time imaging. REYOBIQ is being evaluated for the treatment of recurrent glioblastoma, leptomeningeal metastases, and pediatric brain cancer in the ReSPECT-GBM, ReSPECT-LM, and ReSPECT-PBC clinical trials, respectively. ReSPECT-GBM is supported by an award from the National Cancer Institute (NCI), part of the U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH), and ReSPECT-LM is funded by a three-year $17.6 million grant from the Cancer Prevention & Research Institute of Texas (CPRIT). The Company's ReSPECT-PBC clinical trial for pediatric brain cancer is supported by a $3 million grant from the U.S. Department of Defense's Peer Reviewed Cancer Research Program.

About CNSide Diagnostics, LLC
CNSide Diagnostics, LLC is a wholly owned subsidiary of Cerenome, Inc. that develops and commercializes proprietary laboratory-developed tests, such as CNSide®, designed to identify tumor cells that have metastasized to the central nervous system in patients with carcinomas and melanomas. The CNSide® CSF Assay Platform enables quantitative analysis of the cerebrospinal fluid that informs and improves the management of patients with leptomeningeal metastases.

About Cerenome
Cerenome (Nasdaq: CNSY) is a CNS oncology company advancing an integrated platform that combines precision diagnostics, targeted therapeutics, and artificial intelligence to improve outcomes for patients with central nervous system cancers. The CNSide® CSF diagnostics platform combines cellular and molecular testing to support the detection, characterization, and longitudinal assessment of cancers involving the CNS.

Its lead therapeutic platform, REYOBIQ™ (rhenium Re186 obisbemeda), is being evaluated in clinical trials for leptomeningeal metastases, recurrent glioblastoma, and pediatric brain cancers. The data & artificial intelligence platform is designed to integrate diagnostic, molecular, imaging, and clinical data into actionable insights that support precision oncology and therapeutic innovation.

By integrating commercial diagnostics, targeted therapeutics, proprietary longitudinal data, and artificial intelligence within a single organization, Cerenome is building a differentiated CNS oncology platform designed to improve patient care while creating long-term shareholder value. GRAND RAPIDS, Mich., Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Meritage Hospitality Group Inc. (OTCQX: MHGU), today reported financial results for the third quarter and nine months ended September 27, 2026.

2026 Third Quarter Highlights:

  • Sales were $133.6 million compared to $154.6 million for the same period last year, which included approximately 70 fewer stores in operation.
  • Net (Loss) from Operations was ($6.6) million compared to ($6.6) million for the same period last year. The third quarter of 2026 results included one-time professional fees charges of $2.4 million.
  • Net (Loss) was ($7.7) million compared to ($9.0) million for the same period last year, representing an improvement of $1.3 million.
  • Consolidated EBITDA (a non-GAAP measure) was a loss of ($2.9) million compared to ($4.3) million for the same period last year, representing an improvement of $1.4 million.

“The Company is undertaking a major restructuring of its business and improving store-level profitability, and we believe in the strength of the brand. Wendy’s has a great legacy with proven long-term resilience, and the new senior leadership team is acutely focused on accelerating product innovation, marketing and clear alignment between franchisees and the brand. Wendy’s CEO, Bob Wright, recently announced that breakfast will become optional for Wendy’s franchisees, which is intended to bolster franchisee profitability $200 million. We have taken many actions to optimize our Wendy’s portfolio and expect to see the full extent of these economic benefits realized at the store-level in 2027,” stated Meritage CEO, Robert E. Schermer, Jr.

Furthermore, the Wendy’s brand recently announced “Dave’s Way” which is intended to lead with an operation first turnaround to strengthen its foundation, enhance menu and marketing performance, and modernize how customers experience the brand. “Dave’s Way” is about igniting the energy and distinctiveness that have always made Wendy's special, while positioning the brand and its franchisees for profitable store-level growth as we move forward.

2026 Year-To-Date Highlights:

  • Sales were $407.2 million compared to $472.7 million for the same period last year.
  • Net (Loss) from Operations was ($31.5) million compared to ($7.3) million for the same period last year. The current year included one-time charges of $19.6 million related to one-time professional fees and closing and disposition costs.
  • Net (Loss) was ($30.8) million compared to ($12.9) million for the same period last year.

Third Quarter 2026 and Recent Highlights

  • Exploration: The 2026 Exploration Drilling Program is complete, with more than 16,000 meters of core drilled. In August and then in November 2026, the Company reported new high-grade gold and antimony discoveries and identified a new gold-tungsten zone.
  • Financing update: Perpetua continued diligence and documentation on the $2.9 billion senior secured long-term loan from the Export-Import Bank of the United States ("U.S. EXIM") under the Make More in America Initiative, approved by the U.S. EXIM board on May 21, 2026. The Company continues to advance detailed engineering, long-lead procurement, early works, critical path construction, and execution planning ahead of a final investment and construction decision. Construction Update

Perpetua completed 494,480 work hours during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, with no reportable spills and no serious injuries. Other highlights include:

  • Burntlog Route: Crews advanced construction along the alignment, removed dead timber left by past wildfires, and moved to pioneer roadwork. The year-round access road will give the Project an expanded and upgraded route capable of handling larger loads and equipment.
  • Worker Housing Facility: Treated wood foundations were installed for the kitchen, dining, and recreation modules, and a metal foundation was installed to support the dormitory buildings and the arctic corridor.
  • Powerline: Perpetua is well advanced in procuring key equipment. Substations and transformers are on order, while deliveries of power poles and ancillary equipment continue to the Company's laydown areas in Donnelly and Cascade, Idaho. Power pole installation commenced in October.

Looking ahead, Perpetua will continue to advance critical path work including bridge deliveries for Burntlog Route, installation of the worker housing facility, ongoing powerline procurement and construction, and placing orders for long-lead-time equipment.

New Exploration Results Announced

The 2026 drilling program sought to upgrade in-pit and near-pit inferred resources, extend mineralization along strike, test key underground targets, and follow up on discoveries from the 2025-2026 program. Recent highlights included:

  • Fiddle Discovery: The new Fiddle prospect, located approximately 750 meters south of the permitted Yellow Pine Pit, includes some of the most significant mineralized material encountered at the Stibnite Gold Project to date. Discovery hole SB633 returned 109.7 meters of 3.2 g/t gold and 1.1% antimony. Fiddle adds a new target area with potential to expand the Project's in-pit and near-pit resource base. The Company has since completed significant additional drilling at Fiddle, with assay results expected in the coming months.
  • Clark Tunnel Fault Zone (CTFZ): First announced in August, the CTFZ is located within or adjacent to the southeastern limits of the permitted Yellow Pine Pit. New results announced earlier this month returned near-surface, high-grade gold intercepts from recent drilling, including 25.4 meters of 4.5 g/t gold from 13 meters downhole and 25.0 meters of 2.3 g/t gold from 18 meters downhole. These results follow the drilling announced in August, which included a tungsten discovery in Hole SB597 that returned 21.3 meters of 3.2 g/t gold and 0.9% tungsten from 24 meters downhole.

Near-Term Outlook

Through the remainder of 2026 and early 2027, Perpetua is advancing early works, critical path construction, and detailed engineering for the process plant. Other initiatives include finalizing key construction and equipment contracts. With the 2026 exploration program recently completed, Perpetua expects to announce ongoing exploration results into 2027.

Perpetua Resources Corp., through its wholly owned subsidiaries, is focused on the exploration, site restoration and redevelopment of gold-antimony-silver deposits in the Stibnite-Yellow Pine district of central Idaho. The Stibnite Gold Project is one of the highest-grade, open-pit gold deposits in the United States and holds the only identified domestic reserve of the critical mineral antimony, which is essential to the defense, energy and manufacturing sectors. TORONTO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Organigram Global Inc. (NASDAQ: OGI) (TSX: OGI) (the “Company” or “Organigram”), Canada's #1 cannabis company by market share¹ and a growing global cannabis platform, today announced that on November 11, 2026, it received notification (the “Notification”) from The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”) that it is not in compliance with the minimum bid price requirement under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5450(a)(1) for continued listing on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. The Notification was issued because the closing bid price of the Company's common shares was below US$1.00 per share for 30 consecutive business days. Nasdaq Listing Rule 5450(a)(1) requires listed common shares to maintain a minimum bid price of US$1.00 per share (the “Minimum Bid Requirement”), while Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A) provides that a deficiency exists when the requirement is not met for 30 consecutive business days.

The Notification has no immediate effect on the listing or trading of the Company's common shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. Pursuant to Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A), the Company has 180 calendar days, until May 10, 2027, to regain compliance with the Minimum Bid Requirement. To regain compliance, the closing bid price of the Company's common shares must be at least US$1.00 per share for a minimum of 10 consecutive business days during the compliance period, subject to Nasdaq's discretion to extend this period.

If the Company does not regain compliance by May 10, 2027, it may be eligible for an additional 180-calendar-day compliance period, subject to satisfying applicable Nasdaq requirements, including transferring its listing to the Nasdaq Capital Market. If the Company does not qualify for an additional compliance period, its common shares may become subject to delisting proceedings, subject to applicable appeal rights.

The Company's common shares are also listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange, and the Notification does not affect the Company's listing or compliance status on that exchange.

The facility in London will be optimized for labelling, packaging, and national fulfillment. The Company is regulated by Health Canada under the Cannabis Act and the Cannabis Regulations.

HOUSTON, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- First Horizon Bank (NYSE: FHN) (or "First Horizon") today announced it is working alongside Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Galveston-Houston and AltCap to implement an innovative financing solution to build a new 60,000-square-foot facility that will significantly improve access to food and other services for low-income Houstonians. The new Family Opportunity Center in north Houston will leverage New Markets Tax Credits (NMTC) provided by First Horizon Bank and the Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) AltCap.

Slated to open its doors in 2028, the Family Opportunity Center will feature a market-style food pantry, thrift store, and access to the nonprofit's services, including mental health counseling, parenting classes, rental assistance and job readiness resources. It will also provide space for community and first responders during natural disasters, along with ample warehouse space for food storage.

The total investment for the center, located at 9111 Jensen Drive, is $25 million. To date, Catholic Charities has raised $17.5 million in private and foundation gifts. The NMTC represents nearly 10 percent of the total needed.

Congress established the NMTC to encourage private-sector investment in low-income communities, including the future location of the Family Opportunity Center. Under the program, CDFIs such as AltCap are awarded tax credit allocations from the U.S. Department of the Treasury and deploy them to support projects that deliver measurable community benefits. Investors, including financial institutions like First Horizon Bank, receive federal tax credits in exchange for qualified investments. This investment structure enables community-serving projects, such as the Family Opportunity Center, to access favorable financing and move forward when traditional financing alone may be insufficient.

"We are proud to work alongside Catholic Charities and AltCap to provide financing for the Family Opportunity Center," said Yasmin Huebinger, Houston Commercial Banking Leader for First Horizon Bank. "This investment reflects First Horizon's commitment to strengthening the communities we serve, expanding economic opportunities and driving sustainable growth that benefits families and the broader Houston community."

"As Catholic Charities continues its Building to Serve Capital Campaign, the Family Opportunity Center stands as a testament to what can be achieved when nonprofit organizations, community development partners and financial institutions align resources around a shared vision," said Michael D. Hansen, president and CEO of Catholic Charities. "The cooperation among Catholic Charities, AltCap and First Horizon Bank illustrates how innovative financing can help transform lives and strengthen communities across the Houston region."

"As a CDFI that has been helping to increase access to capital for Houston entrepreneurs and small businesses since 2022, AltCap is excited to demonstrate how we can also support high impact community investments like the Family Opportunity Center using the NMTC Program," said Ruben Alonso III, CEO of AltCap. reitfinancial

A triple net lease is a rental agreement where the tenant pays the base rent plus three main ongoing costs: property taxes, building insurance, and routine maintenance. For investors, this shifts much of the expense and risk onto the tenant, creating a steadier, more predictable income stream for the property owner—similar to renting a furnished home where the renter also pays the bills—making valuation and cash-flow forecasting simpler.

(Nasdaq: OPTX) (“Syntec Optics” or the “Company”), a provider of deep-tech products to industry pioneers connecting and protecting the world, today announced financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Supporting mission-critical applications ranging from low-Earth-orbit satellites and bipartisan connected-battlefield defense platforms to life sciences, Syntec delivered an all-time high revenue of $8.5 million, up 23% year over year, and net income improved by $1.6 million to a positive net income of $0.2 million, compared with a $1.4 million net loss in the prior-year quarter. The quarter’s results reflect Syntec’s expanding role in next-generation bipartisan defense and space technologies, including continued growth in major programs of national importance like Artemis III, low-Earth orbit reconnaissance, satellite collision-avoidance, and AR/VR soldier gear. Gross profit for the quarter increased 127% year over year to $1.9 million. Gross margin nearly doubled compared with the prior-year quarter. Selling, general, and administrative expenses were $1.7 million, reduced by $0.3 million from the prior-year quarter. Adjusted EBITDA was $0.9 million, or 10% of revenue, compared with approximately break-even and an Adjusted EBITDA margin of nearly 0% in the prior-year quarter. 

Beginning this quarter, we are presenting revenue across five end markets: Space Tech, Defense Tech, Life Sciences, AI Data Center, and Other Scientific Instruments. These categories will provide greater visibility into the markets served by our products and the demand drivers affecting our business going forward. Space Tech includes space-related communications, orbital safety, reconnaissance, and rockets. Defense Tech covers bipartisan, cross-administration, proven next-gen AI-driven AR/VR connected battlefield, night-vision, and other soldier gear. Together, Space Tech and Defense Tech represent 64% of our third-quarter revenues and are expected to continue driving our success in subsequent quarters.

Our fastest-growing end market is space technology. Syntec is excited to share that Space Tech revenue increased 117% year over year to $1.3 million. In Q3, Space Tech represented 15% of quarterly revenue and was the fastest-growing segment for the quarter. Our space products support low-Earth-orbiting satellites, debris detection and collision avoidance, reconnaissance, and lunar rocket hardware. In Q3, we announced orders that expand our participation in orbital safety and government satellite reconnaissance. These new product lines broaden our space business across multiple customer programs and mission requirements.

After quarter-end, we announced orders for a new program for our actuator products to support NASA’s Artemis III rockets. This program extends our space portfolio from satellites into hardware supporting lunar missions.

Defense Tech revenues increased 31% year over year to $4.2 million. This represents 49% of quarterly revenue. Our products support AI-enabled AR/VR soldier systems, night vision, missile guidance, and laser targeting products. Announcements during the year included camera and display-window products for military wearable systems, demonstrating expanded participation in customer platforms. Growth across established and newer applications supports our focus on supplying mission-critical products throughout customer program life cycles.

Our Life Sciences revenue increased 12% year over year to $2.7 million, representing 31% of quarterly revenue. Our product lines in this market serve blood diagnostics for early detection of disease, biomedical illumination and visualization, surgical robotics, DNA sequencing, ophthalmology, and veterinary care. These programs provide a substantial revenue base alongside our expanding defense and space base, giving Syntec a more diverse product mix.

AI Data Center revenue was $0.2 million. We expect this category to grow in the coming years as our products are deployed across multiple value chains within the data center. Activities include precision micro-connectors for transceivers and photonic integrated circuits, as well as optics supporting emerging orbital and earth-based fusion energy. A massive energy shortage is predicted by nearly all analysts, and Syntec plans to participate in next-generation products with cutting-edge pioneers. In August, we reported approximately $4.0 million in cumulative orders across the broader AI infrastructure “picks and shovels” opportunity since entering that market roughly two years ago.

Other scientific instruments revenue, which includes products for quantum computing applications, was $0.2 million.

The Company ended the quarter with $14.4 million in cash and cash equivalents, up from $14.0 million at the end of the second quarter. Operating activities generated $1.3 million of cash during the first nine months of the year.  “Our strong cash position gives us the flexibility to invest alongside our customers as their next-generation technologies ramp up to high production volumes for 7-10 year product life cycles,” said Dean Rudy, Chief Financial Officer. “We see an opportunity to build on our momentum in defense and space by expanding our manufacturing capabilities, utilizing our open capacity, and pursuing complementary growth opportunities. Our focus is on translating that opportunity into sustained revenue growth and stronger profitability.”

Filings seek approval for new generation and transmission infrastructure to support growth while delivering benefits for existing customers

ASHLAND, Ky., Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kentucky Power today filed plans with the Kentucky Public Service Commission (PSC) to bring significant new economic development to eastern Kentucky while delivering direct financial benefits to existing customers and protecting them from the costs of serving new large-load customers.

The filings would support TeraWulf's planned Muskie Data Campus in Grayson, Kentucky, and the infrastructure needed to serve it. Over the life of the agreement, the project is expected to provide Kentucky Power customers with more than $500 million in fixed-cost rate offsets and $100 million in winter bill credits for residential customers.

"Our commitment to eastern Kentucky goes beyond providing reliable electricity. We've served these communities for generations, and we want our customers and communities to share directly in the benefits when new investment comes to the region," said Cindy Wiseman, president and chief operating officer of Kentucky Power. "Eastern Kentucky has a tremendous opportunity ahead, and thoughtful growth can strengthen our electric system, support good jobs and attract new investment."

Supporting eastern Kentucky's economic growth

Kentucky Power announced its amended agreement with TeraWulf in October, and today's filings mark the next step in seeking the regulatory approvals needed to move the project forward.

TeraWulf's planned Muskie Data Campus is expected to support up to 1 gigawatt of contracted electric demand in phases by 2029, subject to regulatory approval and construction schedules. To reliably serve that demand, Kentucky Power is seeking approval to construct a new 760-MW combined-cycle natural gas facility next to its Big Sandy natural gas generating unit in Louisa and a new transmission substation in the EastPark Industrial Park area.

The planned Muskie Data Campus also is expected to generate new economic activity through infrastructure investment, construction activity, permanent jobs and new tax revenue for local communities.

Delivering benefits for existing customers

If approved by the PSC, TeraWulf will fund $100 million in winter bill credits for Kentucky Power's residential customers beginning in 2029 and continuing over the first 10 years of the contract.

Kentucky Power signed the White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge, reaffirming its commitment that growth should pay for growth while delivering long-term value for existing customers. Additionally, Kentucky Power's large-load tariff requires data centers to provide financial backing for the cost to serve their projects before they connect to the grid. 

In addition to paying all applicable service charges, TeraWulf has agreed to pay the estimated financing costs associated with construction of the proposed generation facility at Big Sandy. Together, these protections are designed to ensure the costs associated with serving TeraWulf's new demand are paid for by TeraWulf, while allowing new and existing customers to share in the benefits created by the growth.

Today's filings begin the next phase of regulatory review for the proposed agreement and infrastructure. The generation facility and transmission infrastructure each require separate Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity from the PSC. Subject to the PSC's review schedule, decisions on the filings could come as early as mid-year 2027. 

About Kentucky Power
Kentucky Power, with headquarters in Ashland, provides electric service to about 162,000 customers in 20 eastern Kentucky counties, including Boyd, Breathitt, Carter, Clay, Elliott, Floyd, Greenup, Johnson, Knott, Lawrence, Leslie, Letcher, Lewis, Magoffin, Martin, Morgan, Owsley, Perry, Pike and Rowan. Kentucky Power is an operating company in the American Electric Power (Nasdaq: AEP) system. For more information, visit kentuckypower.com.

SAN DIEGO, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Calidi Biotherapeutics, Inc. (NYSE American: CLDI) ("Calidi" or the "Company"), a biotechnology company pioneering the development of targeted genetic medicines, today reported financial and operating results for the three months ended September 30, 2026, and reviewed recent business highlights.

“Throughout the third quarter, Calidi continued to advance its RedTail platform for systemic and local delivery and redefine the potential of oncolytic viruses and genetic medicine,” said Eric Poma, Ph.D., Calidi Biotherapeutics CEO. “In particular, CLD-401 demonstrated remarkable anti-tumor activity with systemic administration in syngeneic tumor models and continues to progress towards the clinic.”

Third Quarter 2026 and Recent Business Developments

  • Presented two posters at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 on October 24, 2026. The presentations showcased new data from the Company’s RedTail platform, a systemically delivered virotherapy platform engineered to selectively target tumors, remodel the tumor microenvironment, and enable high-level expression of therapeutic genetic payloads directly within tumors.
    • Preclinical data on Calidi’s lead program, CLD-401, showed complete tumor eradication in 80% of EMT6 breast cancer tumor-bearing mice versus 0% in the control arm. CLD-401 was engineered for systemic delivery, and new data from an MB49 bladder cancer model show it retains antitumor activity with either systemic intravenous or localized intratumoral administration, supporting flexible delivery approaches across tumor accessibility and disease settings. 
    • Presented preclinical data from Calidi’s in situ T-cell engager (“TCE”) platform, including CLD-501, its TROP-2-targeted candidate, and CLD-502, its EpCAM-targeted candidate.   Following intravenous delivery, the platform generated approximately 10 ng/mL of EpCAM-targeted TCE directly within tumors, and both targeted TCEs demonstrated antigen-dependent, does-responsive T-cell mediated cytotoxicity.
  • Received $1.2 million gross proceeds from an at-the-market registered direct offering that closed on September 18, 2026.
  • Reduced general and administrative expenses by $1.0 million, or 39%, in the third quarter of 2026 versus the same period in the prior year. Reduced general and administrative expenses by $3.6 million, or 42%, in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, versus the same period in the prior year. On November 6, 2026, Calidi executed a restructuring plan, predominantly through a reduction in headcount, that is expected to save $3 million on an annualized basis to extend the Company’s cash runway to reduce costs, extend the Company's operating runway, and preserve capital while pursuing additional financing. 

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Calidi reported a $3.6 million net loss attributable to common stockholders for the third quarter of 2026, compared to a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $10.8 million for the third quarter of 2025, which included a $5.7 million non-cash charge for a deemed dividend on warrants.  There was no such charge during the third quarter of 2026.

Research and development expenses were $2.7 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $2.4 million for the same quarter in 2025.

General and administrative expenses were $1.6 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $2.7 million for the same quarter in 2025.

The Company had $3.9 million in cash and $0.2 million in restricted cash as of September 30, 2026, compared with $5.6 million in cash and $0.2 million in restricted cash as of December 31. 2025.

About Calidi Biotherapeutics

Calidi Biotherapeutics (NYSE American: CLDI) is a biotechnology company pioneering the development of targeted therapies with the potential to deliver genetic medicines to distal sites of disease. The Company’s proprietary RedTail platform features an engineered enveloped oncolytic virus designed for systemic delivery and targeting of metastatic sites. This advanced enveloped technology is intended to shield the virus from immune clearance, allowing virotherapy to effectively reach tumor sites, induce tumor lysis, and deliver potent genetic medicine(s) to metastatic locations.

CLD-401, the lead candidate from the RedTail platform, currently in IND-enabling studies, targets metastatic non-small cell lung cancer, head and neck cancer, and other tumor types with high unmet medical need. Calidi continues to advance its pipeline utilizing the RedTail platform including its novel approach to incorporate in situ T-cell engagers in solid tumors.

Calidi Biotherapeutics is headquartered in San Diego, California. For more information, please visit www.calidibio.com.

IRVINE, Calif., Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cheetah Net Supply Chain Service Inc. (“Cheetah” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq CM: CTNT), a provider of logistics and warehousing services and international trading services, today reported results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 and provided a corporate update.

For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported total revenue of $3,557,805, compared to $361,935 in the same period in 2025, representing an increase of $3,195,870, or 883.0%. The Company recorded an operating loss of $821,890 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to an operating loss of $1,564,479 in the same period in 2025, representing a decrease of $742,589, or 47.5%. The decrease was primarily due to an increase of $237,229 in gross profit and the absence of an impairment loss of $731,307 recognized in the same period in 2025, partially offset by an increase of $287,851 in general and administrative expenses compared to the same period in 2025. The Company recognized other expenses, net, of $1,726,105 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, primarily attributable to a $2,783,884 loss resulting from the change in fair value of acquisition-related contingent consideration asset, partially offset by interest income of $398,232 and other income of $666,508. After accounting for an income tax provision of nil, the Company reported a net loss from continuing operations of $2,547,995, compared to net loss from continuing operations of $1,314,650 for the same period in 2025, representing an increase in net loss of $1,233,345, or 93.8%.

Tony Liu, Cheetah’s Chairman and CEO, commented: “The third quarter of 2026 marked an important step forward in the execution of our business diversification strategy. Following the acquisition of Super International Trading Limited in May, our international trading business demonstrated encouraging momentum, generating approximately $3.56 million in revenue during the quarter. This performance reflects the progress we have made in expanding our business platform and developing new sources of revenue.”

“While our logistics and warehousing business continues to face challenges arising from evolving global trade conditions and cross-border customer demand, we remain focused on optimizing our operating structure and allocating resources toward opportunities that we believe offer greater long-term growth potential. We are encouraged by the progress of our international trading business and will continue to focus on strengthening its operations, expanding business opportunities, and improving operational efficiency.”

“Looking ahead, we remain committed to disciplined capital allocation, prudent financial management, and the pursuit of strategic opportunities that complement our existing capabilities. We believe that our continued efforts to diversify our revenue streams and strengthen our operating platform will position the Company for sustainable long-term growth.”

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Continuing operations – logistics and warehousing business

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported revenue of $nil from its logistics and warehousing services segment, compared to $361,935 for the same period in 2025. The decrease was primarily due to the disposition of Edward and the expiration of TWEW’s legacy customer service contracts during late 2025 and early 2026, which were not renewed on their original terms. As of the date of this release, TWEW is renegotiating logistics and labor services arrangements with customers that had business relationships with TWEW prior to its acquisition, and letters of intent and draft contracts with certain of these customers are in the process of being executed.

The Company also reported cost of revenue of $nil and $317,757 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, representing a decrease of $317,757, or 100.0%, consistent with the corresponding decline in revenue from Edward and TWEW.

Gross profit for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was $nil, a decrease of $44,178, or 100.0%, from $44,178 for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

General and administrative expenses for the Company’s continuing operations-logistics and warehousing services segment decreased by $90,368, or 84.1%, to $17,068 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $107,436 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease was mainly due to the disposal of Edward in 2026.

Continuing operations – international trading

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported revenue of $3,557,805 from its international trading segment, all of which was generated by Super International Trading Limited (“Super International”), which we acquired on May 27, 2026. The increase was primarily due to the expansion of the Company’s international trading business following the acquisition of Super International.

The Company also reported cost of revenue of $3,276,398 and $nil for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, representing an increase of $3,276,398, all of which was attributable to Super International, consistent with the corresponding increase in international trading revenue.

Gross profit for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $281,407, an increase of $281,407, from $nil for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

General and administrative expenses for the Company’s continuing operations - international trading segment increased to $23,349 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $nil for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was mainly due to the commencement of the Company’s international trading operations following the acquisition of Super International on May 27, 2026.

Continuing operations – Corporate Unallocated Operating Adjustments

General and administrative expenses for the Company’s continuing operations- corporate unallocated operating adjustments segment increased by $354,870, or 51.1%, to $1,048,697 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $693,827 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was mainly due to travel and entertainment expenses and legal and accounting fees and other general and administrative expenses.

Share-based compensation expenses were $14,183 and $76,087 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, representing a decrease of $61,904, or 81.4%.

Interest income from continuing operations was $398,232 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $244,776 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, representing an increase of $153,456 or 62.7%. The increase was primarily due to an increase in average outstanding loan balances as the Company made additional loans to third parties, resulting in higher interest income.

Interest expense incurred from our continuing operations was $6,961 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, which decreased by $888, or 11.3%, from $7,849 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, mainly due to the continued amortization of our long-term borrowings and lower credit card and premium finance interest.

Net other income from continuing operations was $666,508 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $12,902 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, representing an increase of $653,606, or 5,065.9%. The increase was primarily driven by higher foreign exchange gains resulting from currency rate fluctuations.

The Company’s receivable from withdrawal of investment deposit of $41,762,995 as of September 30, 2026, represents RMB 280,000,000 contributed by Naiside to a PRC investment fund in January 2026 and repayable in full by Shanghai Kesheng on or before December 30, 2026. The receivable is denominated in Renminbi and remeasured at each reporting date. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recognized an unrealized foreign exchange gain of $652,422 on this receivable. Excluding this non-cash gain, the Company’s loss from continuing operations before income taxes of $2,547,995 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 would have been approximately $3,200,417.

Other expense from the change in fair value of acquisition-related contingent consideration asset was $2,783,884 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $nil for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

As a result of the above factors, the Company had a net loss of $2,547,995 from continuing operations for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a net loss of $1,314,650 for the same period of 2025.

Nine Months 2026 Financial Results

Continuing operations – logistics and warehousing business

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported revenue of $92,700 from its logistics and warehousing services segment, compared to $1,195,860 for the same period in 2025. The decrease was primarily due to the disposition of Edward and the expiration of TWEW’s legacy customer service contracts, as described above.

The Company also reported cost of revenue of $72,833 and $1,060,526 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, primarily reflecting labor and logistics costs for TWEW and ocean freight service costs incurred by Edward.

Gross profit for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $19,867, a decrease of $115,467, or 85.3%, from $135,334 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

General and administrative expenses for the Company’s continuing operations-logistics and warehousing services segment decreased by $179,749, or 50.8%, to $173,757 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from $353,506 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease was mainly due to lower operating and administrative expenses following the disposal of Edward, as well as ongoing cost control initiatives.

Continuing operations – international trading

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported revenue of $4,426,714 from its international trading segment, of which $208,909, or 4.7%, was attributable to Cheetah, and $4,217,805, or 95.3%, was attributable to Super International, which the Company acquired on May 27, 2026. The increase was primarily due to the expansion of the Company’s international trading business following the acquisition of Super International.

The Company also reported cost of revenue of $4,125,807 and $nil for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, representing an increase of $4,125,807 including $199,409 attributable to Cheetah and $3,926,398 attributable to Super International, consistent with the corresponding increase in international trading revenue.

Gross profit for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $300,907, an increase of $300,907, from $nil for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

General and administrative expenses for the Company’s continuing operations-international trading segment increased to $43,433 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from $nil for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was mainly due to the acquisition of Super International.

Continuing operations – Corporate Unallocated Operating Adjustments

General and administrative expenses for the Company’s continuing operations- corporate unallocated operating adjustments segment increased by $275,462, or 12.2%, to $2,529,043 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from $2,253,581 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was mainly due to an increase in travel and entertainment expenses and other general and administrative expenses.

Share-based compensation expenses were $42,547 and $102,716 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, representing a decrease of $60,169, or 58.6%.

Interest income from continuing operations was $814,069 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $725,094 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, representing an increase of $88,975 or 12.3%. The increase was primarily due to an increase in average outstanding loan balances as the Company made additional loans to third parties, resulting in higher interest income.

Interest expense incurred from our continuing operations was $21,460 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, which decreased by $3,261, or 13.2%, from $24,721 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, mainly due to lower average outstanding balances under long-term borrowings and premium finance arrangements.

Net other income from continuing operations was $1,669,286 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $42,658 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, representing an increase of $1,626,628, or 3,813.2%. The increase was primarily driven by higher foreign exchange gains resulting from currency rate fluctuations.

During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recognized an unrealized foreign exchange gain of approximately $1,631,708 related to the receivable arising from the withdrawal of the investment deposit. Excluding this non-cash gain, the Company would have incurred a loss from continuing operations before income taxes of approximately $4,719,313 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Other expense from the change in fair value of acquisition-related contingent consideration asset was $2,783,884 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $nil for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

As a result of the above factors, the Company had a net loss of $3,093,215 from continuing operations for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a net loss of $2,581,087 for the same period of 2025.

Liquidity and Going Concern Considerations

The Company reported a net loss of approximately $3.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and net cash used in operating activities of approximately $2.5 million. As the Company continues to integrate its newly acquired international trading business and develop its logistics and warehousing service business, the Company may continue to incur operating losses and generate negative cash flow. These factors were considered in management’s evaluation of the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern, together with the mitigating factors described below.

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of approximately $14.5 million and a working capital balance of $87.1 million. In addition, the Company had a receivable from withdrawal of investment deposit of $41.8 million and loans receivable from third parties of approximately $29.5 million, which can be sufficient for the Company to support its ongoing business operations and meet the obligations in the future.

Management has evaluated the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern in accordance with ASC 205-40, Presentation of Financial Statements – Going Concern. This evaluation considered the Company’s current financial condition, expected cash flows, obligations due within the next 12 months, and available sources of liquidity.

The Company is working to further improve its liquidity and capital sources primarily by generating cash from operations, pursuing debt financing, and, if needed, seeking financial support from its principal stockholder. If necessary to fully implement its business plan and sustain continued growth, the Company may seek additional equity financing from outside investors. Based on the current operating plan, management believes that the aforementioned measures collectively will provide sufficient liquidity to meet the Company’s liquidity and capital requirements for at least 12 months from the issuance date of its consolidated financial statements.
